questions.question: The emergency air line supplies air to the:
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) has two jobs. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.

questions.question: Why should you do pre-trip inspection steps in the same order every time?

options.text: Because you will be less likely to forget to check something
Because it is required by law

questions.correctAnswerText: Because you will be less likely to forget to check something
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way each time. This habit helps you remember to check everything important.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Move quickly before other vehicles get into the lane you wish to occupy.
Move slowly, in case another vehicle is in the lane you wish to occupy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly, in case another vehicle is in the lane you wish to occupy.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives other drivers time to move out of your way or warn you with their horn. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: If turning to avoid a hazard:

options.text: You should not brake as it may cause the wheels to lock.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should not brake as it may cause the wheels to lock.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while turning quickly to avoid a hazard. Braking can cause your wheels to lock and your vehicle to skid out of control.

questions.question: A combination vehicle has ____ air line(s).
questions.explanation: Every combination vehicle has two air lines: the service line and the emergency line.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Sit in the cab and call for help.
Exit the cab and walk away from the tracks.
Motion for another driver to push your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the cab and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, exit immediately and walk away from the tracks. Call emergency authorities for help.

questions.question: People working on a disabled vehicle:

options.text: Are probably aware of the roadway.
May be distracted by the repair and not pay attention to the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be distracted by the repair and not pay attention to the roadway.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on a disabled vehicle on the roadside. They may be focused on the repair and not watching traffic.

questions.question: A driver should test the tractor protection valve by:

options.text: Releasing air with the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Releasing air with the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Test the tractor protection valve by letting the air supply charge fully, turning off the engine, then pressing the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to its emergency position when air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: When starting an engine during a pre-trip inspection, the driver should:

options.text: Place the engine in first gear.

questions.explanation: Check your engine during the pre-trip inspection. After starting the engine, listen for any unusual noises.

questions.question: Where must placards be placed?

options.text: Only on the front of a vehicle
On the front, back and both sides of a vehicle
Only on the driver's side of a vehicle
Only on the passenger's side of the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, back and both sides of a vehicle
questions.explanation: When carrying hazardous materials that require placards, place identical placards on the front, rear, and both sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: An open car window in cold weather may mean the driver is:

options.text: Using the heat in their vehicle.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impaired driving. Drivers who have drunk too much, are tired, are using drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. An open window in cold weather is a warning sign of impaired driving.

questions.question: While driving, you should:

options.text: Not use mirrors because they distract you.
Only use mirrors when there is traffic.

questions.explanation: You must always know what is around you. Check your mirrors regularly to stay aware of your surroundings.

questions.question: Which is NOT an example of a dangerous driver?

options.text: A driver who did not scrape ice off the windshield
A driver of a station wagon with items blocking the back windows

questions.explanation: Drivers with blocked vision are a hazard. Examples include drivers with ice on their windshields, drivers with large items blocking windows, and drivers of rental trucks who are not used to limited rear visibility.

questions.question: When connecting glad hands, match the colors. Service lines are usually:
questions.explanation: When coupling glad hands, connect matching glad hands together. Colors help drivers avoid mistakes. Service lines are usually blue, and emergency lines are usually red.

questions.question: Escape ramps can be used to:

options.text: Leave the highway and enter a two-lane road.
Stop runaway vehicles on steep hills going downward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop runaway vehicles on steep hills going downward.
questions.explanation: Escape ramps are built on steep downhill sections to safely stop runaway vehicles. They have a long bed of loose, soft material and sometimes an uphill slope.

questions.question: Set the trailer air supply control to "emergency" to test:
questions.explanation: Always test the trailer emergency brakes before driving. Make sure the trailer rolls freely first. Then test the brakes by pulling out the trailer air supply control or setting it to "emergency." Pull forward slightly with the tractor and check that the trailer does not move.

questions.question: To prevent surge when stopping, you should NOT:

options.text: Keep steady pressure on the brakes.

questions.explanation: To reduce surge in a tank vehicle, brake slowly and keep steady pressure on the brakes. Do not release the brakes too early. Brake well in advance and keep a larger distance from other vehicles.

questions.question: When driving in fog, the safest choice is to:
questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see the road, other drivers, and hazards. Avoid driving in fog whenever possible.

questions.question: When turning, when should you turn off your turn signal?
questions.explanation: When turning or changing lanes, signal early and keep signaling the whole time. Turn off your signal once the turn or lane change is done.

questions.question: If you think you will be late, you should:
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, manage your stress. If you realize you will be late, take a deep breath and accept the situation. Drive at a safe speed.
